label: agent-study

fixtures.name: trend-control
fixtures.note: regime-switching drift + AR(1) residual: the desk's own positive control, and the fixture the trend claim is about

fixtures.name: mean-reverting
fixtures.note: OU around a level with a 16-bar half-life: the structure a fade is supposed to trade

fixtures.name: sweep-rich
fixtures.note: the same level plus a raid every ~100 bars that is absorbed: sweep-rich on purpose, because a setup that happens twice a series cannot be measured

fixtures.name: vol-clustered
fixtures.note: GARCH(1,1): quiet stretches and shock clusters, the one property of real returns no null generator has

fixtures.name: seasonal
fixtures.note: a drift that depends only on the UTC hour: clock structure and nothing else

fixtures.name: regime-labelled
fixtures.note: the WP3 labelled control: bull/bear/range, useful for the trend agent's direction rather than its probability

fixtures.name: null-driftless
fixtures.note: driftless random walk: no structure of any kind

fixtures.name: null-phase
fixtures.note: phase-randomised: linear structure survives, non-linear does not — the strictest null

fixtures.name: null-shuffled
fixtures.note: block-shuffled returns: the marginal distribution kept exactly, every temporal dependence destroyed

agents.reason: all 7 gates passed on seasonal and the pooled nulls

notes: Every agent states a probability, and the probability is its own measured hit rate for this exact setup, shrunk toward the MEASURED random-entry baseline for the same stop and horizon (see alpha/edge.ts). The gate is whether that number beats the baseline on the fixture and fails to beat it on the nulls.

The 'baseline' column is the random-entry hit rate with identical geometry AND the same direction as each view, measured causally on windows that had closed by the decision bar. It is not 1/(1+RR): with a time horizon most setups expire, and on these M15 fixtures the coin-flip rate measures 0.10–0.34 depending on the fixture's volatility, so judging an agent against 1/3 would have measured the calendar. It is also direction-matched on purpose: a realised driftless path still ends 25–35σ from its start, buys then do better than sells, and an agent that is simply long on such a path would otherwise show an edge it does not have (measured: +8.6 points on pure noise before the comparator was matched).

Paper trading runs the agent through the SHIPPED position manager and the executed-policy simulator (alphaStrategy in research/harness.ts): the stop, targets, partials, break-even and trail are the desk's, and only the direction and the probability come from the agent. It is reported for EVERY agent with a home fixture, enabled or not — a measured zero is evidence — and it is a smaller sample by construction. The ledger beside it says which layer refused each decision.

An agent that fails its gates is left DISABLED. Its code, its fixture and its numbers stay in the repository: a measured negative result is a result, and the next person to have the same idea should find it here.
